facts.statement: Condorraptor was one of the earliest large theropod dinosaurs found in South America, discovered in Lower Jurassic rocks in Argentina.
facts.quote: It was among the earliest large South American theropods, having been found in Lower Jurassic strata of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation in the Cañadón Asfalto Basin of Argentina.

facts.statement: The species Condorraptor currumili was first described by scientists in 2005.
facts.quote: The type species, described in 2005, is Condorraptor currumili.

facts.statement: The genus name means 'robber from Cerro Condor' and the species name honors Hipolito Currumil, the landowner where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Its genus name means 'robber from Cerro Condor', referencing a nearby village, while its species name, currumili, is named after Hipolito Currumil, the landowner and discoverer of the locality.

facts.statement: The original type specimen of Condorraptor was a juvenile individual approximately 4.5 meters long and weighing about 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: The type specimen was a juvenile that was about 4.5 metres long and it weighed about 200 kg.

facts.statement: Condorraptor is considered one of the largest early South American theropods, reaching an estimated length of about 7 meters, though it was initially thought to be only 4 to 5 meters long.
facts.quote: Condorraptor fue uno de los primeros terópodos sudamericanos más grandes, habiéndose encontrado en lo sestratos del Jurásico Medio de la Formación Canadon Asfalto en Argentina, medía aproximadamente 7 metros de largo, aunque en un principio se pensó que solo llegaba a medir entre 4 a 5 metros.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Condorraptor is cataloged as MPEF-PV 1672, which is a left tibia bone.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Condorraptor es MPEF -PV 1672, una tibia izquierda.

facts.statement: Additional remains referred to the species include vertebrae, teeth, ribs, hip fragments, femurs, a fourth metatarsal, and a foot phalanx.
facts.quote: Restos adicionales, MPEF-PV 1673 a 1697 y MPEF-PV 1700 a 1705, también se han referido a la especie, incluyendo vértebras , dientes, costillas y fragmentos de chuerones, huesos parciales de cadera, fémures , un metatarsiano IV y una falange del pie.

facts.statement: In 2007, a larger articulated skeleton comprising about 70% of the bones was discovered at Cerro Condor.
facts.quote: En el 2007, también en Cerro Cóndor, se encontró un ejemplar articulado de mayor tamaño y con un 70 % de sus huesos.

facts.statement: The team that found the articulated skeleton included Oliver Rauhut, Magali Cárdenas, Leandro Canessa, Mariano Caffa, José Luis Carballido, and Pablo Puerta.
facts.quote: El equipo que lo encontró estaba integrado por el mismo Oliver Rauhut, Magali Cárdenas, Leandro Canessa, Mariano Caffa, José Luis Carballido y Pablo Puerta.

facts.statement: Condorraptor lived during the Middle Jurassic period, approximately 162 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 162 millones de años, en el Calloviense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Research by Benson in 2010 classified Condorraptor as a piatnitzkysaurid megalosauroid and the closest relative to Piatnitzkysaurus.
facts.quote: Benson (2010) found it to be a piatnitzkysaurid megalosauroid and the sister taxon of Piatnitzkysaurus, a finding supported by later studies.

facts.statement: Condorraptor is classified within the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Piatnitzkysauridae

facts.statement: Condorraptor is characterized by a posterior notch between the fibular condyles, the absence of the medial proximal part of the tibia, and a deep lateral fossa on the cnemial crest.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por la presencia de una incisura posterior entre los cóndilos de la fíbula y la parte medial de proximal de la tibia ausente y una profunda fosa en lateral de la cresta cnemial

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Condorraptor feature a pleurocoel located in the anterior portion at the posteroventral angle of the parapophysis.
facts.quote: las vértebras cervicales con pleurocelo en la porción anterior ubicada en el ángulo posteroventral de la parapofisis

facts.statement: A large nutrient foramen is present on the lateral side of the ischial peduncle in the ilium of Condorraptor.
facts.quote: un gran foramen nutricio en el lado lateral del pedúnculo isquiático en el ilion

facts.statement: The fourth metatarsal of Condorraptor has a distinct step on the dorsal and distal articular surface.
facts.quote: el cuarto metatarsiano con un paso en la cara dorsal y distal de la cara articular

facts.statement: Due to the fragmentary nature of the initial discovery, the classification of Condorraptor remains incomplete, though it is known to be a basal tetanuran likely related to Piatnitzkysaurus.
facts.quote: Debido a lo fragmentario del primer descubrimiento, la clasificación de este dinosaurio es incompleta, se sabe que fue un tetanuro basal, probablemente emparentado con Piatnitzkysaurus encontrado en el mismo sitio.

facts.statement: A fragmentary partial skull described in 2007 is possibly attributed to Condorraptor based on its size, locality, and tetanuran characteristics, despite differences from Piatnitzkysaurus cranial material.
facts.quote: En 2007, Rauhut describió un cráneo parcial fragmentario, MPEF 1717, de la Formación Canadon Asfalto. Debido al tamaño del cráneo, la localidad, las características del tetanuro y las diferencias con el material craneal de Piatnitzkysaurus, es posible que pertenezca a Condorraptor.

facts.statement: The species is based on a tibia and an associated partial skeleton that may belong to the same individual.
facts.quote: Está basado en una tibia, con un esqueleto parcial asociado que puede pertenecer al mismo individuo.

facts.statement: The genus Condorraptor belongs to the parent group Piatnitzkysauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Piatnitzkysauridae

facts.statement: Condorraptor is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Condorraptor lived between the Toarcian and Bajocian stages, from 180.4 to 168.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Bajocian (180.4 to 168.6 million years ago)
